The Google Store serves the Pixel tech-spec page in HTML — 8.8 KB of text on pixel_10_specs. Its class names are obfuscated and change between deploys, so there is no stable hook on a row; what IS stable is the shape, an

naming a group ('Battery and charging', 'Dimensions and weight') followed by the

lines that are that group's facts. There are no labels at all, so every group is filed under its heading and the fact is picked out of the sentence by its unit — which is exactly why a unit is required here: '204 g' is a weight and '24+ hour battery life' is not, and only the unit tells them apart. The page also quotes prices; the crawler copies only whitelisted schema fields, so no price can reach a record. Discovery is the awkward part: sitemap_in.xml publishes 140 URLs and only five end in _specs, all of them watches or earbuds — not one Pixel phone. The phone spec pages exist and answer (pixel_10_specs, pixel_10a_specs, pixel_11_specs, pixel_10_pro_fold_specs all serve a full sheet), they are simply not listed. So the slug is built from the model name and the page must name the model itself before it is used. Two shapes are served under the same URL pattern and only one is a spec sheet. pixel_10_specs is a single product's sheet, headings then facts. pixel_11_pro_specs is a COMPARISON: a two-column table putting Pixel 11 Pro beside Pixel 11 Pro XL, with both machines' values as sibling cells in one row. Read as a single product it would attribute the XL's battery to the Pro, so the compare markup is detected and the page yields nothing — the same call enrich_appliances_html.py makes for a Daikin page that tabulates three variants. The 9 Pixel Pro/Pro XL records are therefore left empty rather than filled from a column that may belong to the other phone. pixel_10_pro_xl_specs is separately unusable: it answers 200 but its delivered text carries no spec value at all.
